question: Where was the 2024 Regional World Children's Day commemorated by UNICEF from 15 to 17 November?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Victoria Falls, Zimbabwe**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 2024 Regional World Children's Day was commemorated by **UNICEF** at Victoria Falls, Zimbabwe, from 15 to 17 November.
 
• This event aimed to advocate for the rights and well-being of children globally, emphasizing the importance of child welfare and education.
 
• Victoria Falls, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, was chosen due to its global significance and the symbolic representation of cross-border collaboration.
 
• The event included discussions, workshops, and initiatives focused on addressing challenges faced by children, particularly in Africa and other developing regions.
 
• It brought together policymakers, activists, and children to emphasize the theme of equal opportunities and sustainable futures for all children.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UNICEF's World Children's Day:**

 
 
• World Children's Day, celebrated annually on November 20, is an initiative by UNICEF to promote awareness and action on child rights globally.
 
• The day marks the adoption of the Declaration of the Rights of the Child (1959) and the Convention on the Rights of the Child (1989).
 
• The focus is on ensuring access to education, healthcare, and equal opportunities for children worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Victoria Falls:**
 
 
• Located on the Zambezi River at the border of Zambia and Zimbabwe, Victoria Falls is one of the world's largest waterfalls.
 
• It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a major tourist attraction due to its breathtaking beauty and ecological significance.
 
 
 
• **Key Challenges for Children in Africa:**
 
 
• High rates of poverty, malnutrition, and lack of access to quality education and healthcare.
 
• Child labor, early marriages, and conflicts remain significant barriers to child development in the region.
 
 
 
• **UNICEF's Role:**
 
 
• UNICEF works to provide humanitarian aid, advocate for child rights, and implement programs focusing on health, nutrition, and education.
 
• The organization collaborates with governments, NGOs, and communities to create sustainable impacts for children worldwide.
